answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because bridge only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, whisper is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any plume approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
